title: What Is a Tummy Tuck Without Muscle Repair Called?
meta_description: Often called a mini or skin-only tummy tuck, though names vary. How it differs from a full tummy tuck, who it suits, recovery and what it can't fix.
excerpt: A tummy tuck without muscle repair is often called a mini tummy tuck, though names vary. What it removes, how it differs from a full tummy tuck, who it suits, what recovery looks like and what photos of it show.
quick_answer:
What is a tummy tuck without muscle repair called?

Often a mini tummy tuck or a skin-only tummy tuck, though neither name is exact. A mini removes loose skin and fat below the belly button through a shorter incision, leaving a scar of about 3 to 6 inches (Cleveland Clinic). Some surgeons also tighten the lower muscles, so ask. With separated muscles, ask about a full tummy tuck.

sources.title: Tummy Tuck
quotes: Tummy tuck surgery, also known as abdominoplasty, removes excess fat and skin and, in most cases, restores weakened or separated muscles creating an abdominal profile that is smoother and firmer.
A tummy tuck is not a substitute for weight loss or an appropriate exercise program.
Although the results of a tummy tuck are technically permanent, the positive outcome can be greatly diminished by significant fluctuations in your weight.
For this reason, individuals who are planning substantial weight loss or women who may be considering future pregnancies would be advised to postpone a tummy tuck.

Make an opening and move your belly button into position.
Panniculectomy: A panniculectomy removes hanging skin and fat from your lower abdominal region.
This procedure doesn’t tighten muscles, move your belly button or address fullness in your upper abdomen.

It could take up to up to three months to see the final result.
In addition, the scar will continue to improve further for up to one year.

sources.title: Tummy Tuck Scar
quotes: Full tummy tuck: The scar for a standard tummy tuck usually spans your abdomen, from hip bone to hip bone, just above your pubic area.
You may also have a scar around your belly button.
Mini tummy tuck: A mini tummy tuck is for people who have a small amount of excess fat and tissue beneath their belly button.
It’s about the length of a C-section scar (between 3 inches and 6 inches).

sources.title: Diastasis Recti
quotes: It’s a common condition that affects 6 in 10 women after childbirth.
An abdominal gap wider than 2 centimeters is considered diastasis recti.
Your provider will use their hands and fingers to feel your abdominal area for gaps and muscle tone.
Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
See how many fingers can fit in the gap between your right and left abdominals.
If you feel a gap of two or more finger widths, discuss your concerns with your healthcare provider.
They can confirm you have diastasis recti and recommend treatment.

sources.title: Understanding the different types of tummy tucks
quotes: It improves only the area below the belly button, removing lax skin and strengthening muscles in the lower stomach.
Some advantages of having a mini tummy tuck are that it uses a smaller incision, often costs less and requires less recovery time than a full tummy tuck.
Most people can return to work one to two weeks after surgery and resume more vigorous activities in about five to six weeks.
The trade-off is that its results are limited to the lower abdomen.
A traditional tummy tuck is the most common type of abdominoplasty, focusing on both the upper and lower abdomen.
Most patients can return to nonstrenuous work after a couple of weeks, but it takes around three months to fully recover from a tummy tuck.
Standard tummy tucks are best for men and women who want to firm and tighten the area above and below the belly button.
They will then remove excess skin and fat from your midsection and repair separated or weakened abdominal muscles.
